answer.rationale: Competitor price cut creates immediate churn risk in price-sensitive SMB segment. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_44 indicates enterprise prospects have higher conversion quality through sales-assisted paths—suggests protecting enterprise segment from price competition while responding to SMB pressure. Memory_86 shows onboarding improvements drive durable adoption but won't address immediate price sensitivity. A small_guarded_test of promotional pricing on at-risk SMB accounts balances defense of near-term revenue with preservation of pricing power. Risk: promotional pricing can erode unit economics and create expectation anchoring that persists post-competition. However, this is lower risk than losing accounts entirely or diluting brand positioning through broad discounting. Small test scope allows measurement of churn prevention ROI before broader rollout. Enterprise segment should remain isolated from promotional pressure (memory_44 quality conversion suggests they're less price-sensitive).
